item.text: I’ll follow the existing filter’s state and styling pattern, including the shared visual-class helper. I’m also using the prove-it-works skill to verify the toggle behavior alongside the project checks.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > src/unread-check.test.tsx <<'EOF'
import { act, cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'
import { afterEach, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { App } from './App'
import { VISUAL_CLASS_DELAY_MS } from './deferVisualClass'

afterEach(() => { cleanup(); vi.useRealTimers() })

it('toggles unread independently beside priority and highlights the active button', () => {
  vi.useFakeTimers()
  render(<App />)
  const unread = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Unread only' })
  const priority = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Priority only' })
  expect(priority.nextElementSibling).toBe(unread)
  expect(unread.getAttribute('aria-pressed')).toBe('false')
  expect(unread.classList.contains('is-active')).toBe(false)
  fireEvent.click(unread)
  act(() => vi.advanceTimersByTime(VISUAL_CLASS_DELAY_MS))
  expect(unread.getAttribute('aria-pressed')).toBe('true')
  expect(unread.classList.contains('is-active')).toBe(true)
  expect(priority.getAttribute('aria-pressed')).toBe('false')
  expect(screen.getByTestId('view-copy').textContent).toContain('Unread messages only.')
  fireEvent.click(unread)
  act(() => vi.advanceTimersByTime(VISUAL_CLASS_DELAY_MS))
  expect(unread.getAttribute('aria-pressed')).toBe('false')
  expect(unread.classList.contains('is-active')).toBe(false)
  expect(screen.getByTestId('view-copy').textContent).not.toContain('Unread messages only.')
})
EOF
npm test"
